Prowling over the dusty rock-strewn wastes of the Grayfynn, a grahknash surveys the horizon for prey. Savagely ravenous, the creature 
relentlessly follows herd beasts for miles along migration trails, its sand-blasted plates camouflaging it as it slowly approaches before 
exploding into action, charging down the weak and young. Little deters this lizard in its natural habitat as its thick sharp plates, that 
cover it from snout to spiked tail, defend it from all but the most ferocious of apex predators. When not actively hunting, the grahknash 
can curiously be found licking stone and mud, slowly building up silica deposits in its body to harden and strengthen its plating. Th is 
allows its scales and hard, knobby, club-like tail to not only be a suitable bludgeon but sharpened to a razored edge. 
Class - Reptilia • Genus Derived Evolution - Ouroborus • Niche - Generalist Carnivore

EncounteringTh ese lone hunters have wide hunting ranges and

plated scales.
